symptom: The loop produced a bare-UUID commit message (fd91251) despite validateCommitMessage being the documented defense — the guard's 'guarantee' (system:commit-message-guard.json constraints) is insufficient.
evidence: Observed 2026-11-10 during push-divergence reconciliation: git log showed commit fd912512431c4e79c72e7865dc691d9932d39a46 with message 'c9b2331d-10ed-41fc-888d-68f7a5bee002' (bare UUID v4), author craighckby-stack <242091616+craighckby-stack@users.noreply.github.com>, committed 2026-11-10T06:56:49Z, touching only postmortems/self/main/system:push-divergence.json (1 file, +3/-1). This was committed ~90s after the loop was rebooted at 06:55:11 (POST /api/self-enhance/reboot). The existing guard postmortem (system:commit-message-guard.json) states validateCommitMessage runs before every git add -A in pushCurrentState (both paths ~L698 and ~L778) and rejects empty/whitespace/bare-UUID first lines. Yet fd91251 landed. Either (a) the postmortem-recording path (recordFailure writing to postmortems/) commits via a path that does NOT go through pushCurrentState, bypassing validateCommitMessage, or (b) validateCommitMessage's regex /^[0-9a-f]{8}-...$/i missed this UUID, or (c) the commit was made before validateCommitMessage was added and only detected at boot. Hypothesis (a) is most likely: the postmortem-recording path appears to git-commit its JSON write directly rather than routing through pushCurrentState. Manually amended fd91251 -> ed9af89 with message 'self-enhance: mark push-divergence postmortem resolved after operator merge-back of loop-187 orphans' to unblock the push (a bare-UUID commit is not a valid message for the push-target gate).
constraints: The commit-message-guard (system:commit-message-guard.json) has a SCOPE GAP: it only guards commits that route through pushCurrentState. The postmortem-recording path (and possibly other direct git-commit sites in the loop) bypass it. Required fix for a future audit: (1) audit ALL git commit sites in src/lib/pipeline/ for validateCommitMessage coverage — not just pushCurrentState; (2) move the guard to a git pre-commit hook (.git/hooks/pre-commit) or a wrapper around child_process exec git commit so it covers every commit site by construction, not by convention; (3) the boot-time detector is necessary but not sufficient — it only catches the artifact after it lands. Until the guard covers all commit sites, the loop can produce bare-UUID commits undetected between boots. Related: the keepalive cron prompt (cron job 520064) and the dev-server daemonizing finding (system:sandbox-process-sweep.json) — both are operational knowledge that a fresh session must re-derive if these postmortems are lost.
resolution: Resolved by operator (constructive gate, 2026-11-11): (1) Installed .githooks/commit-msg (versioned in-repo, activated via `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`) — git itself invokes it with the final message file for EVERY `git commit`, so coverage is by construction, not convention. Note: commit-msg is the correct hook, not the pre-commit suggested in constraints — pre-commit runs before the message is composed and cannot see it; commit-msg receives the proposed message as $1. Rules mirror validateCommitMessage (reject empty/whitespace first line, reject bare-UUID first line); re-tested live: bare-UUID and empty commits exit 1, valid messages pass. (2) Removed the repo's only --no-verify (lessons-markdown.ts commitLessonsFile) so no commit site can bypass the hook; its constant message always passes the gate. (3) Full audit of git-commit sites at fix time: push-target.ts L1178 (guarded L1165), L1288 (guarded L1270), L968 amend (guarded L945), merge-back.ts L318 (constant template, now hook-covered), lessons-markdown.ts (constant message, now hook-covered after --no-verify removal). All five sites constructively covered. Residual risk documented: core.hooksPath is local git config — a fresh clone or full .git rehydration must re-run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`; deleting .githooks/ is visible in git status so it cannot vanish silently. The in-process validateCommitMessage guards remain as the first layer (they give structured reject reasons to the loop); the hook is the backstop that makes bypass structurally impossible rather than conventionally unlikely.
